A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 37-page versions of the same DADO paper. Their text, equations, figures, table and Appendix A can be matched reliably, including the rotated protein-structure graphics.

before.justification: v2 reports original computational optimization experiments on synthetic functions and protein property predictors, plus decomposition-robustness and runtime results in Appendix A.9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original computational experiments and their outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithm 1 and the appendix retain the same factorized search distribution, message-passing value functions and weighted maximum-likelihood updates. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic problems and seven protein datasets: AAV, Amyloid, Gcn4, TDP-43, GB1, ynzC and CreiLOV. Appendix coverage, including larger synthetic spaces and training on the bottom 50% of assay labels, is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding optimization experiments retain the same EDA, FDA and PPO comparators where evaluated. Appendix comparisons using EDA alone and predictive-model analyses using the Naive NN comparator also retain their membership.

E3.justification: Training iterations, sampling budgets, hyperparameter sweeps, model configurations, cross-validation, holdout procedures and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The interval-label revision does not document a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: Appendix A.9 retains the same scaling analyses, GB1 contact-threshold case study, graph-mutation robustness experiments, bottom-50% training analyses and runtime study. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 4 and captions for Figures 1–3 and A2–A6 replace '95% confidence interval' with '95% interval.' This changes uncertainty labeling, while run counts, significance tests and displayed bands remain unchanged. No changed estimator or additional runs are documented. Figure A6b still labels its bands '95% CI,' leaving the revision incomplete.

E6.justification: The plotted curves, rankings, p-values and Table 1 entries are retained. For example, Figure 2b still reports p = 4.45e-12, and the L = 400 runtimes remain 139.5 minutes for EDA and 114.2 minutes for DADO.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendices A.1–A.5 retain the same mathematical definitions, message-passing equations, lower-bound reasoning and maximum-entropy derivation. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and discussion retain the same claims about exploiting junction-tree decomposability for efficient distributional optimization and demonstrating its utility on protein property predictors.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning optimization efficiency, high-variance value functions, decomposition robustness and applicability limits remain unchanged. The non-overlap observation in Section 4 is retained; its interval terminology changes under E5.

D1.justification: Dataset descriptions, architectures, optimizer settings, preprocessing, computational-resource information and code-access instructions remain the same in Section 6 and Appendices A.6–A.9.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning relative to FDA, reinforcement-learning policy optimization and Bayesian optimization.

P1.justification: Language edits are confined to the interval terminology in nine passages and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Paragraph organization, section order and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Most result plots are embedded at lower raster resolution in v3, reducing detail under substantial enlargement while retaining readable labels and the same graphical content. Edited captions undergo limited line reflow. Figure placement, panel organization, axes, legends and Table 1's layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Replacing 'confidence intervals' with 'intervals' for the displayed sample-score bands reduces the risk of confusing score dispersion with confidence in an estimated mean. This is a limited reporting improvement: interval construction remains unspecified, and Figure A6b still says '95% CI.' The scientific evidence is unchanged. Plot downsampling reduces enlargement detail but preserves readability and the reported findings.
